name: Demi Guard to Lapel Guard
summary: Demi Guard to Lapel Guard releases the foot-on-lapel configuration while preserving useful gi grips and leg frames, returning the bottom player to broader lapel-guard options.
description: Demi Guard to Lapel Guard in gi BJJ: learn the starting controls, movement sequence, defensive reactions and recovery options for a connected lapel-guard exchange.
overview:
Demi addresses the passer who comes forward. When distance opens again, the guard player can stop insisting on that close knee-line configuration and retain a more general lapel guard. The source introduction explains the relationship between forward pressure and leaving the worm configuration: [Keenan's introduction](https://jiujitsux.com/courses/keenans-lapel-encyclopedia/lesson/16-1-introduction-to-the-demi-guard/).

This recovery ends at [[Positions/Lapel Guard]], whose own choices include [[Transitions/Lapel Sweep to Back]], [[Transitions/Lapel Omoplata Entry]] and [[Transitions/Lapel Triangle Setup]]. Those are subsequent exchanges with their own entry requirements, not direct finishes from Demi. Keeping usable fabric and a leg barrier is what makes that continuation possible.

attacker.name: Demi Guard to Lapel Guard Attacker
attacker.description: Execute Demi Guard to Lapel Guard with the right starting controls, a stable destination and a clear recovery when the attempt is blocked.
attacker.overview: You begin in Demi Guard bottom and keep a useful lapel grip as the passer moves away from the close pressure exchange. Replace the foot-on-tail configuration with ordinary leg frames while staying in front. The aim is a usable lapel guard from which a separate attack can be arranged.
key_principles: Keep useful fabric control during the change.
Use the space created by the passer's retreat.
Replace foot contact with a working leg barrier.
Stay facing the passer while changing the connection.
Treat a later attack as a separate setup.
setup_requirements: You are in Demi Guard bottom.
The passer has created enough distance to change the foot configuration.
A useful lapel grip remains available.
Your legs can remain between the two players during the change.

execution_steps.description: Recognize that the passer has reduced forward pressure and made room to change the close foot-on-lapel configuration.
Keep control of the lapel without pulling it so tightly that it prevents the leg movement needed for guard recovery.
Move the foot off the tail only while arranging a leg frame that keeps the passer from advancing directly to your torso.
Adjust your hip angle so your knees remain between the players as the passer changes distance or direction.
Confirm that you have usable fabric control and a guard barrier without requiring the defining Demi foot-on-tail placement.
Choose a lapel-guard sweep or submission setup only after confirming its additional grips and leg position in the recovered guard.

common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Contest the frame change before it settles

common_errors.error: Dropping the lapel while changing the foot
common_errors.consequence: The intended lapel-guard continuation loses its main control.
common_errors.correction: Retain a useful grip while replacing the leg barrier.

common_errors.error: Removing the foot without a replacement frame
common_errors.consequence: The passer can close the gap directly to your torso.
common_errors.correction: Arrange another guard frame during the foot change.

common_errors.error: Keeping the old wrap tighter than the movement permits
common_errors.consequence: Your own leg cannot move into the recovered guard.
common_errors.correction: Release only the tension that obstructs the change.

common_errors.error: Letting the passer circle behind your knees
common_errors.consequence: The fabric grip no longer protects a viable guard angle.
common_errors.correction: Follow with your hips to keep the knees between the players.

common_errors.error: Chasing a back take before recovering guard
common_errors.consequence: Missing controls expose the guard change to a pass.
common_errors.correction: Establish the destination and then meet the next technique's setup requirements.

training_progressions.description: You are in Demi Guard bottom. With a cooperative partner, identify the required grips and leg contacts, then reset without applying pressure.
Perform the listed sequence slowly with a cooperative partner. Pause at the change of lapel or foot control and reset on any joint discomfort.
Let the partner use this response: Keep the existing configuration contained. Practice keeping a safe base or guard when it blocks the attempt, then reset.
Start at the stated origin with light resistance. Stop and reset at a stable destination, a counter, or a request to release; do not continue through a bound knee.

flashcards.question: What must remain useful when leaving Demi for Lapel Guard?
flashcards.answer: Keep a usable lapel grip and a leg barrier while replacing Demi's specific foot-on-tail configuration.

flashcards.question: Which passer reaction creates space for this recovery?
flashcards.answer: The passer reducing forward pressure or moving away can create room to change the close Demi foot configuration.

flashcards.question: What should replace the foot as it leaves the lapel tail?
flashcards.answer: A working leg frame must continue protecting the space between the players while you recover broader lapel control.

flashcards.question: When should you start a back take after this guard change?
flashcards.answer: Begin only after the recovered lapel guard supplies the additional grips and angle required by the separate back-take technique.

flashcards.question: How should your hips follow a circling passer during the recovery?
flashcards.answer: Adjust the hip angle to keep your knees between your torso and the passer rather than letting them circle behind the leg barrier.

attacker.safety_considerations: Use controlled pressure with a cooperative partner when learning the lapel path. Release fabric immediately on a tap, verbal stop or discomfort. Do not rotate against a knee held by the lapel, and stop the drill when a stable landing is reached.

defender.name: Demi Guard to Lapel Guard Defender
defender.description: Recognize and respond to Demi Guard to Lapel Guard while protecting balance, remaining frames and a safe recovery route.
defender.overview: You are the passer as the bottom player changes the close Demi configuration into broader lapel control. Removing their foot from the tail does not mean all fabric control has disappeared. Preserve your balance while contesting the remaining grip and leg frames, and recognize whether a guard still separates your torsos.
key_principles: Recognize the change of collar, lapel and foot controls early.
Keep a usable base or leg barrier while contesting the movement.
Choose a response that fits the current controls rather than a lost grip.
Release any connection that binds a knee during movement.
Identify the resulting position before continuing the exchange.
recognition_cues: The guard player keeps lapel contact as you move away.
The foot leaves the tail while another leg frame replaces it.
Their hips follow your direction to keep both knees in front.

defensive_options.when_to_use: When the bottom player cannot make room for a new frame
defensive_options.if_successful: The attempted reconfiguration stalls in Demi Guard.
defensive_options.risk: Pressuring without balance can load the Demi sweep.

defensive_options.action: Contest the frame change before it settles
defensive_options.when_to_use: As the foot leaves the lapel tail
defensive_options.if_successful: The bottom player must restore their starting guard.
defensive_options.risk: A reach that loses base opens a sweep rather than stopping the change.

defensive_options.action: Clear the grip and legs through an exposed gap
defensive_options.when_to_use: Only if the guard player has abandoned both useful fabric and leg frames
defensive_options.if_successful: You settle a pin after clearing the recovered-guard attempt.
defensive_options.risk: Remaining lapel tension or a leg frame can still stop the pass.

favorable_outcomes.how: Keep the existing configuration contained. The attempted reconfiguration stalls in Demi Guard.
Contest the frame change before it settles. The bottom player must restore their starting guard.
Clear the grip and legs through an exposed gap. You settle a pin after clearing the recovered-guard attempt.

common_errors.error: Responding after the new controls are established
common_errors.consequence: The attacker completes the movement before the response affects it.
common_errors.correction: Recognize the listed cues during the control change.

common_errors.error: Turning against a knee still bound by the lapel
common_errors.consequence: The joint cannot follow the body movement freely.
common_errors.correction: Release binding tension and reset rather than forcing the turn.

common_errors.error: Ignoring the position left after the attempt
common_errors.consequence: You continue with a response intended for a guard that has already changed.
common_errors.correction: Check the actual leg and upper-body controls before the next action.

flashcards.question: Why is a foot leaving the lapel tail not proof of a completed escape?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player may retain useful lapel control and replace the foot with other leg frames, leaving a different guard.

flashcards.question: What two barriers must you clear to counter this recovery with a pass?
flashcards.answer: Clear the remaining fabric control and the leg frames before settling upper-body control from the side.

flashcards.question: What can happen if you drive forward carelessly during the change?
flashcards.answer: You can reload the original Demi connection and give the guard player an elevation opportunity instead of stopping the recovery.

training_progressions.description: From the stated origin, have the partner begin slowly. Call out a listed recognition cue, then release and reset.
Keep the existing configuration contained. Use light resistance and stop when the response succeeds or the connection becomes uncomfortable.
Let the partner choose whether to continue or recover. Respond using the available controls; stop at the resulting stable position and name both players' roles.
